title: gawkbot: the open source Grok Bot, bots you (almost) control
excerpt: gawkbot is the open source Grok Bot. gawkbots automate your menial work via AI models and build you microapps to manage the outcome, so that you have a false sense of control.
content_html:
open source bots that (almost) serve you

gawkbots automate your menial work via AI models and build you microapps to manage the outcome, so that you have a false sense of control.

Runs on your machine, with your keys. No account, no cloud, no per-seat pricing.

Download GitHub  ★

THE BOTS

They do the boring part.

You find out afterwards, on a dashboard.

Every bot runs on your machine as its own worker, with a shell, a browser, and a working directory of its own. It uses the tools you allow it, nothing more, and then it does the thing you have been putting off since March.

  • filer Filed forty-one expense reports overnight. Left you a chart to look at.
  • reconciler Matched the invoices against the bank. Two did not agree. Both now do.
  • triager Triaged your inbox before you woke up. Ninety-three down to four.
  • scheduler Booked the six meetings you kept not booking. Invitations are out.
  • chaser Chased everyone who owed you a reply. Got four. Still working on Dave.
  • tidier Renamed nine hundred files to the convention you described once, badly.

MICROAPPS

It is already done.
Here is an app about it.

You talk to one bot at a time. Mention another and yours goes off to consult it rather than dragging it into your conversation. Ask for something menial and it tends to be finished before you have described it properly. Then it builds you a microapp, so there is somewhere to click.

Can someone do the expense reports?

They were filed at 04:12. All forty-one of them.

FILER CONSULTED 2 BOTS

reconciler Matched them against the bank. Two did not. Both fixed.

triager Pulled the receipts out of your inbox.

I built you an app to look through them.

APPROVE ALL Review 3

Did I need to approve any of that?

The card charges, yes. They are in the app, waiting for you.

PERMISSIONS

Trust your bots with less over time.

This is the part that is not a joke. An agent with your credentials and a browser is a real risk, and the honest posture is to grant it as little as possible for as long as possible. The defaults below are the actual defaults.

WHAT IT ACTUALLY DOES

  • Runs on your machine, with your keys. There is no gawkbot cloud in the path, and no account to create. Point it at a local model and nothing leaves at all.
  • Every send, commit, purchase, and delete is gated behind an approval you have to click. Approval is per action, not a blanket grant, and it does not persist.
  • Each bot works in its own directory with its own tool allowlist, so what a bot can touch is per bot rather than per workspace. Your credentials never leave your machine.
  • Every tool call is written to a local log you can read. If a bot did something, there is a line for it.
  • Permissions shrink by default. A grant you stop using expires rather than accumulating quietly.

OPEN SOURCE GROK BOT

The open source Grok Bot.

gawkbot is an open source Grok Bot: a team of always-on AI bots that runs on your own machine instead of a vendor's cloud. It is free, it uses the coding agent you already pay for (Claude Code, Codex, or a local model), every external action waits for your approval, and it builds you a microapp so you have something to look at.
